theater: 希臘中部塞薩利與溫泉關

battle.name: 加拉太戰爭
battle.theater: 希臘中部塞薩利與溫泉關
battle.brief: 公元前189年，埃托利亞同盟雇用數千名加拉太傭兵與羅馬共和國在希臘本土再戰。執政官尼亞斯·曼利烏斯·武爾索率軍在塞薩利擊潰傭兵，逼埃托利亞於溫泉關投降。真正決定戰局的是直刃鐵劍、標槍與盾甲，兵器卡上的月牙劍只餘形制上的遠親。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 公元前189年的希臘本土，羅馬共和國與埃托利亞同盟再度開戰。羅馬方面由執政官尼亞斯·曼利烏斯·武爾索率領遠征軍，骨幹是執政官軍團，輔以同盟城邦與亞細亞屬地提供的援軍，軍隊由海路抵達馬其頓，再沿埃格納提亞大道南下，在安菲波利斯與溫泉關一帶維持據點。埃托利亞同盟一方以聯盟城邦的輕裝步兵與同盟騎兵為主，突擊力量則交給由北高盧與多瑙河上游招來的高盧人、加拉太人傭兵團，這支部隊人數不多但以近身砍殺兇猛著稱。馬其頓的珀爾修斯與埃托利亞有共同的利害，但雙方並未公開結盟；亞該亞同盟則自居仲裁者姿態，實質上觀望；迦太基與希臘諸城保持商業往來，卻沒有一方公開介入。戰爭的本質是羅馬要把「解放希臘」的說法落實為實際控制，埃托利亞則要保住它在中部希臘的山地據點與港口。
countriesEn: The war of 189 BC was fought in mainland Greece between the Roman Republic and the Aetolian League, with a body of Gallic and Galatian mercenaries hired by the Aetolians doing much of the close fighting. On the Roman side the expedition was led by the consul Gnaeus Manlius Vulso, built around the consular legions and the contingents supplied by allied cities of Greece and Asia; the column landed in Macedonia and moved south along the Via Egnatia, holding positions around Amphipolis and the approaches to Thermopylae. The Aetolian League fielded the light infantry and skirmishing cavalry typical of its hill country and used the hired northerners as a shock force, small in numbers but feared in close combat. Macedon under Perseus shared an interest in resisting Rome without becoming a formal partner, and the Achaean League posed as a neutral arbiter while waiting to see who would win. Carthage and the Greek cities kept their commercial ties but no one intervened openly. The substance of the conflict was whether the Roman claim to have freed Greece would be converted into actual control: Rome wanted the Aetolian mountain strongholds and the harbours of central Greece, and the Aetolians wanted to keep the position they had built in the interior.
people: 執政官尼亞斯·曼利烏斯·武爾索是這場戰爭的決定人物。他在前一年已奉命接管希臘戰線，率遠征軍在塞薩利迎擊傭兵，把以裸身長刀衝鋒著稱的加拉太人逐退；其後轉向圍城作戰，安菲波利斯之圍以封鎖河道與斷絕糧道完成，馬其頓守軍獲准帶走武器離城，可見他把重點放在補給線而不是強攻。提圖斯·昆克提烏斯·弗拉米尼努斯以和談者身分在溫泉關接待埃托利亞代表，他的外交手段與武爾索的軍事壓力互相配合：先把埃托利亞從盟軍中孤立，再迫其接受條款。與武爾索同任執政官的普布利烏斯·科爾奈利烏斯·西庇阿非利加努斯當時在非洲對付敘法克斯與敘耳古尼人，與希臘戰事沒有直接關係。傭兵一方的指揮官，李維記作布倫努斯，此人與前225年率高盧人入意大利、以及前390年洗劫羅馬的同名人並非一人，不應混為一談。埃托利亞方面沒有留下清晰的戰場指揮姓名，只知同盟將領仍以拖延議價為務；真正推動停戰的是羅馬元老院與執政官派出的使團
peopleEn: The decisive figure was the consul Gnaeus Manlius Vulso, who had already been given command of the Greek theatre. He met the hired Gauls in Thessaly and drove back an enemy famous for charging with long swords and almost no armour, then turned to blockade work: the investment of Amphipolis was completed by closing the river and cutting the supply road, and the Macedonian garrison was allowed to withdraw with its arms, which shows that his priority was the line of supply rather than a storming assault. Titus Quinctius Flamininus appeared in the same year as the negotiator who received the Aetolian surrender at Thermopylae; his diplomacy and Vulso's pressure were two halves of one operation, since the Aetolians were first cut off from their allies and only then forced to sign. The other consul of the year, Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus, was in Africa dealing with Syphax and the Numidian campaign and had no direct part in the fighting in Greece. Livy names the commander of the mercenaries Brennus, who must not be confused with the Brennus who led the Gallic invasion of Italy in 225 BC, nor with the one who sacked Rome in 390 BC. The Aetolian side left no clear name for its own commander in the field, only that the leaders kept stalling through negotiation; the political force behind the settlement lay with the Roman Senate and with the envoys the consuls sent out.
kits: 兵器卡上的埃及月牙劍，是前1500年前後青銅時代的單刃外彎砍刀，弧度順著前臂，砍中甲胄時不必拔刃再揮第二擊。它的形制並未在古典世界消失，而是以科佩斯一類彎刃短刀的形式在東方與北方延續，義大利南部盧卡尼亞人與薩姆尼特人使用的彎刀也屬同一思路；但到公元前189年，希臘與義大利戰場的主流已是直刃鐵劍，羅馬在第三次馬其頓戰爭前後開始裝備的直身雙刃短劍成為標準配備，埃托利亞的希臘步兵用短劍與標槍，馬其頓與塞琉古系的長槍兵用薩里沙長槍，雙方都大量攜帶青銅或鐵製標槍。防護方面，羅馬用弧面大盾配分段甲或鎖子甲，埃托利亞輕步兵用小圓盾與皮甲，高盧傭兵用高身大盾、鎖子甲並戴有尖角的頭盔。攻城與運輸方面，羅馬遠征軍每日築營，依靠工程兵操作攻城塔與填壕器材，圍城以封鎖河道、斷糧道為主，糧秣與攻城器械由地中海海運抵馬其頓，再轉陸路送入希臘內陸
kitsEn: The card shows an Egyptian khopesh, a single edged outward curving blade of the bronze age, made around the fifteenth century BC: the curve follows the forearm, so that a blow which lands need not be wrenched free before the second stroke. The shape did not vanish from the classical world but survived in the curved short swords of the east and the north, such as the kopis, and the same thinking is visible in the falcata carried by the Lucanians and Samnites of southern Italy. By 189 BC, however, the standard of the battlefield in Greece and Italy was the straight iron sword; the Roman straight double edged gladius, coming into use around the Third Macedonian War, was becoming standard equipment, Aetolian hoplites carried the short sword and the spear, the Macedonian and Seleucid phalanx used the long sarissa, and both sides carried bronze and iron javelins in numbers. On protection the Romans used the large convex shield with segmentary or mail armour, the Aetolian light infantry the small round shield and a leather corselet, and the Gallic mercenaries tall rectangular shields, mail, and helmets with projecting spikes. For siege and supply the Roman expedition encamped every day, relied on its engineers for towers and works, and preferred blockade and starvation to direct assault: at Amphipolis they sealed the river and cut the road so that grain could not enter, and rations and siege equipment came by sea to Macedonia and then inland by pack animals and wagon train.
tactics: 埃托利亞的戰法是小國山地國的典型打法：輕步兵以小盾、投槍與弓箭在前，騎兵在兩翼反覆掠擾，遇強敵就退入山嶺，重裝兵線盡量避免在平原地對撞。雇用高盧傭兵正是要補上正面衝擊力的缺口，這支部隊以長刀近身砍殺、盾牌遮蔽身體著稱，衝鋒時幾乎不披重甲，戰力多靠士氣與奪來的戰利品。羅馬方面沿用軍團的縱隊戰法：步兵採百夫隊與大隊編制，先以標槍齊射削弱敵陣，再以劍盾近戰鞏固陣線，騎兵在關鍵時刻投入，以整齊的縱隊衝擊敵軍側翼。遠征軍的另一個重點是圍城而非野戰，安菲波利斯之圍靠封死歐拉克斯河與切斷糧道完成，守軍被允許帶走武器離城，等於用封鎖取代強攻。外交同樣是戰術的一環，弗拉米尼努斯在溫泉關先談判、後施壓，把埃托利亞從其盟軍中逐個孤立，再配合軍方壓力迫其接受條款
tacticsEn: The Aetolian way of fighting was that of a small hill state: light troops with small shields, javelins and arrows in front, cavalry working the flanks and falling back whenever a formed body came on, and a refusal to commit heavy infantry to a frontal clash in the open. Hiring Gauls was meant to fill the gap in shock power, for that force was known for close work with the long sword, for fighting behind its shields, and for charging with little body armour, its strength depending on morale and on what it could take. The Romans fought in the old legion manner, infantry organised in centuries and cohorts, throwing javelins in mass to soften the enemy before closing with sword and shield, and committing the cavalry at the decisive moment so that a coherent column struck the flank. Beside the battle, siege was part of the method: the investment of Amphipolis was completed by closing the Eurax and cutting the supply road, and the garrison was allowed to leave with its arms, which saved the Romans a costly assault. Diplomacy was a third instrument, Flamininus negotiating at Thermopylae to isolate the Aetolians from their allies one by one before the military pressure forced the terms.
data: 可核對的數字不多，且多出於李維的敘述。埃托利亞一方雇用的加拉太傭兵，李維記作約四千人，並與埃托利亞部隊合流作戰；羅馬投入希臘戰線的遠征軍在數千人至一萬之間，以步兵為主，騎兵約數百。戰事橫跨數個戰役季，自公元前191年阿佩馬條約之後展開，至公元前189年埃托利亞正式投降為止。地理上，羅馬隊伍自義大利南部的布蘭迪西翁渡海抵達地拉那，再沿埃格納提亞大道南下至安菲波利斯與溫泉關，陸海合計超過一千公里。值得對照的是公元前192年埃托利亞企圖策反駐義大利高盧傭兵的事件：數千名高盧人被說動後轉而進攻克路西烏姆，最後由執政官弗拉米尼努斯擊退，說明羅馬對這一類手段並非毫無警覺
dataEn: The record is thin, and the figures that survive come mostly from Livy. The Gallic mercenaries hired by the Aetolians are given as about four thousand, fighting alongside Aetolian troops; the Roman force committed to Greece ran from several thousand men up to about ten thousand, infantry in the main with some hundreds of cavalry. The campaign covered more than one campaigning season, opening after the Treaty of Apamea in 191 BC and closing with the formal Aetolian surrender in 189 BC. Geographically the Roman column came from Brundisium in southern Italy, crossed the sea to Dyrrhachium, and then followed the Via Egnatia south to Amphipolis and Thermopylae, well over a thousand kilometres by sea and land together. A useful comparison is the Aetolian attempt of 192 BC to turn the Gallic soldiers in Roman service in Italy: several thousand of them were induced to march on Clusium and were defeated by Flamininus, which shows that Rome was not taken by surprise the second time round.
cause: 戰爭的起因是埃托利亞同盟在希臘中部擴張得太快。埃托利亞在對抗馬其頓與其他同盟城邦的鬥爭中取得山區與港口，塞琉古王安提柯三世看準這股力量能為自己開闢第二戰線，於公元前192年與埃托利亞簽約，使羅馬在對安提柯的戰爭中多出一個敵人。阿佩馬條約簽訂後，羅馬視埃托利亞為必須懲戒的對象，元老院與執政官授權遠征軍進軍希臘追究其責任。埃托利亞則把高盧傭兵當成翻盤的最後一張牌：一方面用高盧人的兇悍挽回士氣，另一方面希望在義大利同時拉開另一條戰線。羅馬對此並非沒有防備，前192年克路西烏姆之役已破解過一次同類陰謀，公元前189年再出現高盧軍團時，羅馬的應對不再是尋求開闢地的會戰，而是把分割、包圍與外交三者並用
causeEn: The war began because the Aetolian League had expanded too fast across central Greece. Having taken mountain strongholds and harbours in the struggle against Macedon and the other league states, the Aetolians were recruited by Seleucid king Antiochus III to open a second front, and the alliance of 192 BC gave Rome a second enemy in the war against Antiochus. Once Apamea had been signed the Aetolians were treated as a power that had to be punished, and the Senate and the consuls authorised an expedition into Greece to hold them accountable. The Aetolians in turn made the Gauls their last card: the mercenaries were meant both to restore morale in the field and to open a second front in Italy at the same time. Rome was not unaware of that scheme, having broken a similar plot at Clusium in 192 BC, and when the Gallic host appeared again in 189 BC the Roman answer was no longer to seek a set piece battle in the open but to combine separation, blockade and negotiation.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果，是埃托利亞同盟喪失了作為希臘獨立勢力的資格。公元前189年投降之後，羅馬得以在中部希臘安置軍團，希臘各城的所謂自由實際上由羅馬的駐軍與使者決定；同盟殘餘的勢力在公元前146年亞該亞戰爭中隨科林斯的陷落一起被清除，希臘的自主命運至此告一段落。另一層影響在兵制與財政：羅馬自此不再解散遠征軍，馬其頓在公元前148年被改為行省，部隊與戰利品大量滯留希臘，國力因而不斷膨脹。埃托利亞與馬其頓大量雇用高盧人作戰的做法，則成了希臘化世界僱傭兵政治的樣板，日後加利太傭兵出現在小亞細亞與敘利亞的戰場上時，外界已知如何評價這些北方來客。對武器史而言，這場戰役也標記着青銅時代弧刃砍刀的退位：公元前189年的希臘戰場上，真正決定勝負的是直刃鐵劍、標槍、盾與攻城器械
impactEn: The outcome of the war was the loss by the Aetolian League of its standing as an independent power in Greece. After the surrender of 189 BC Rome was able to station legions in central Greece, and the freedom of the Greek cities came to mean whatever the Roman garrison and the Roman envoys decided; the last of the League's strength was swept away with Corinth in the Achaean War of 146 BC, and the autonomy of the Greek states effectively ended. A second consequence lay in the military and fiscal order: the legions were no longer disbanded after a campaign, Macedon was turned into a province in 148 BC, and troops and plunder stayed in Greece, so the power of the Roman state grew. The Aetolian and Macedonian practice of hiring Gauls also became the model for mercenary politics in the Hellenistic world, and when Galatian mercenaries later appeared in the battlefields of Asia Minor and Syria, observers already knew how to judge those northern visitors. In the history of arms the campaign marks the retirement of the bronze age sickle blade: on a Greek battlefield in 189 BC what decided the issue was the straight iron sword, the javelin, the shield and the siege works.
result: 公元前189年，埃托利亞同日雇來的加拉太傭兵被羅馬遠征軍擊潰，四千餘人的武裝在塞薩利與希臘中部作不出有效抵抗，隨後潰散或被遣返，僅少數被羅馬收編。走投無路的埃托利亞同盟在溫泉關與弗拉米尼努斯談成投降，承認羅馬在希臘的裁判地位；羅馬隨即解除對同盟城邦的圍困，戰事以埃托利亞同盟的失敗告終。這場戰爭的記載偏少，保存下來的主要是李維《羅馬自建城以來史》第三十八卷中關於高盧傭兵與溫泉關談判的部分，因此確切的起訖月份與傭兵被擊潰的地點只能由後人推估：一般認為戰鬥發生在公元前189年的夏末至秋季，投降亦在同年之內完成，戰爭列表因此把這場衝突記為單一年度的戰役
resultEn: In 189 BC the Gallic mercenaries hired by the Aetolians were beaten by the Roman expedition. Four thousand men in arms could not make an effective stand in Thessaly and in central Greece; they scattered or were sent home, and only a few were taken into Roman service. Cornered, the Aetolian League negotiated a surrender with Flamininus at Thermopylae and accepted the Roman right to arbitrate Greece, the Roman blockade of the Aetolian cities was then lifted, and the campaign ended in defeat for the League. The written record of this war is scanty: what survives comes mainly from Book 38 of Livy's Ab Urbe Condata, dealing with the Gallic mercenaries and the negotiations at Thermopylae, so the exact months of the campaign and the place where the mercenaries were broken can only be reconstructed. The fighting is generally placed in the late summer and autumn of 189 BC, with the surrender completed within the same year, which is why the list of wars records the conflict as a single year campaign dated to 189 BC.
